history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 48 -- PASS. Audited HEAD 9f31512 (code in e0f8847; 9f31512 adds only Build notes to the sprint file). The sprint file was re-read fresh at HEAD, including the 2b amendment (9ed74f4) and the Build notes. Every check below ran on a clean `git archive e0f8847` export, not on the primary checkout, which still holds the operator's uncommitted self-dependency.

Req 1 -- MET. Re-derived independently. Tracked files under scripts/, templates/ and .claude/ at e0f8847, minus the npm pack --dry-run list: launcher_test.js, permission-gate-repro.js, permission-gate-repro-mc-commit.js, verify-tarball.sh. Every path-shaped reference in every shipped file was then checked against the pack list. The only unshipped references are:
- .claude/role-claims.json and settings*.json: runtime state/config, never executed.
- scripts/build.js and scripts/tool.js: hypothetical examples in comments.
- fixture.js: a selftest temp file that check_user_said_guard.py writes itself.
- launcher_test.js: in check_user_said_guard.py:97 as a scan EXCLUSION set, not an invocation, plus README and comments.
- verify-tarball.sh: pipeman.md:35, which is conditional ("if it exists in this repo").
- state.js and setup.*: prose or comments.
No call site was missed and no comment-only mention was miscounted. The list matches Build notes entry by entry.

Req 2 -- MET, with a sprint-file finding (below). There is NO v0.2.24 tag, locally or on origin (git tag -l shows v0.2.2 as the only v0.2.2* match; ls-remote shows zero matches). The baseline is therefore npm pack fully-completely@0.2.24. Its file list is IDENTICAL to npm pack --dry-run at its registry gitHead 8ff3988, checked by me. File-list diff, published 0.2.24 -> e0f8847:
  > scripts/check_user_said_guard.py
  > scripts/check_user_said_history.py
  > scripts/verify-release-content.sh
There are no removals. role-claims.json, verify-tarball.sh, launcher_test.js and permission-gate-repro*.js are all absent. Content changes are CHANGELOG.md, package.json, scripts/install.js (Req 2b) and scripts/baselines/user-owned-content.json. The baseline file is untouched by this sprint (git diff 1bdcbe9 e0f8847 -- scripts/baselines/ is empty); its only change since 8ff3988 is Pipeman's routine post-publish regeneration, 8090d9c. check-staleness.js reports OK through 0.2.24.

Req 2b -- MET. The install.js diff is three FRAMEWORK_OWNED entries plus a comment, nothing else. launcher_test.js exits 0 (ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED) on the clean export.

Req 3 -- MET. smoke_test.sh is unchanged. In-repo, on the clean export: exit 0, ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED. Fresh install of the packed 0.2.25 candidate (npm init, npm install of the tgz, npx fully-completely): all three files are present in scripts/, verify-release-content.sh keeps mode 755, and no dev-only tooling was installed. Installed smoke_test.sh exits 0 both without and with git init.
Falsification: the identical recipe against published 0.2.24 exits 1 with "SMOKE TEST FAILED: check_user_said_guard.py --selftest ... can't open file .../scripts/check_user_said_guard.py". The defect reproduces on 0.2.24 and is gone on the candidate.

Req 4 -- MET. The version is 0.2.25, and npm view reports 0.2.24 as current today. The CHANGELOG entry names finding 15, the three files and the two-list fix, with no freeze or roadmap language. Its "no change to the smoke test itself" statement is accurate.

Req 5 -- MET. `git show e0f8847:package.json` has no dependencies key. The operator's self-dependency is still uncommitted in the working tree, as the user chose. Pipeman publishes from a clone, so that is not a release risk.

Findings (none block):
1. [LOW, sprint-file defect, routed to Master Controller] Req 2's acceptance criterion cannot be satisfied as literally written. It names a v0.2.24 tag that does not exist, and its "package.json/CHANGELOG.md only" content clause predates 2b and did not account for Pipeman's baseline regeneration. I judged it by its evident intent: published 0.2.24 as the baseline, which is stronger than a tag would be, plus the 2b install.js change, plus the pre-existing baseline file. That substitution is recorded here openly, not silently absorbed.
2. [LOW, UNOWNED, first report, routed to Master Controller] launcher_test.js reads FRAMEWORK_OWNED with the regex /'([^']+)'/g, so any comment in that array with an odd number of apostrophes silently mis-pairs every entry after it. The existing comments pass only because their apostrophes happen to pair. Dev Team found this and correctly left it out of scope. No decision is on record for it, and with the freeze nobody will own it. Master Controller should record it as accepted or not.

No Human Prerequisites beyond those already in the sprint file: the user's own real-time publish authorization in Pipeman's session.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 48 round 2 -- PASS. Audited HEAD 1fd31f7 (code in 76fd27a; 1fd31f7 adds only Round 2 Build notes).   > scripts/check_user_said_history.py

There are no removals, and no role-claims.json, verify-tarball.sh, launcher_test.js or permission-gate-repro*.js. Content changes: CHANGELOG.md, package.json, install.js, baselines table -- all within the override's allowed set.
Round 2 addition, vs published 0.2.25: the file lists are IDENTICAL. Content differs only in CHANGELOG.md, package.json and the baselines table. The package.json diff is only "version" 0.2.25 -> 0.2.26 and the removed dependencies block naming fully-completely ^0.2.24.
Also checked: published 0.2.25 is byte-identical to my round-1 audited e0f8847 in every file except package.json. The self-dependency was the only thing that leaked; nothing else unaudited shipped in 0.2.25.

Req 3 -- MET. In-repo smoke_test.sh exit 0 (ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED), and worktree_test.sh exits 0. For a fresh install of the packed 0.2.26 (npm install of the tgz, then npx fully-completely), the installed smoke_test.sh exits 0.

Req 4 -- MET. The version is 0.2.26, and npm view reports 0.2.25 as current. The 0.2.26 entry names the unintended self-dependency, says how it got there (packed from a working checkout, not the reviewed commit), says 0.2.26 is 0.2.25's intended content without it, and says to upgrade from 0.2.25. It has no freeze or roadmap language, and the 0.2.25 entry is untouched. I measured the entry's dedupe claim independently: a fresh `npm install fully-completely@0.2.25` then `npm ls --all` shows "fully-completely@0.2.25 deduped", and there is no nested node_modules. The claim is accurate.

Req 5 -- MET. `git show 76fd27a:package.json` has no dependencies key. `git status --short` in the primary checkout is empty, so the leak source is gone.

Req 6 -- MET. baselines:check exits 0 ("through 0.2.25"). The table gained 0.2.25 for all 7 user-owned paths. I recomputed each sha256 from the actual published 0.2.25 tarball bytes, and all 7 match the table.

Upgrade path rehearsal (LiveQA owns the live version): published 0.2.25 plus the installer, then the packed 0.2.26 tgz plus the installer. Result: "Upgraded 0.2.25 -> 0.2.26", "Already present, unchanged (58)", with no modified or conflict lines. npm ls shows a single fully-completely@0.2.26 with nothing nested, and the installed package.json has no dependencies key. The installed smoke_test.sh exits 0.

Findings: none against the code. For Pipeman and LiveQA: the audited code is clean, and round 1's defect was in how it was packed. The round-2 criteria already make the byte comparison of package.json against the audited commit the deciding check, and that is the check that catches a repeat.

Round-1 QA1 finding 2 (launcher_test.js quote pairing) is now owned: Master Controller recorded it as out of scope and a backlog item (round-2 Out of Scope). It is no longer unowned.

target_index=1 | target_event=audit | target_ts=2026-09-29T19:14:40+00:00 | Correction to QA1's round-1 Req 5 evidence. The sentence "Pipeman publishes from a clone, so that is not a release risk" stated as fact something I never verified: it was an expectation drawn from pipeman.md, not a measurement. It proved false. 0.2.25 was packed from the primary checkout (registry gitHead 03b3ab8), and the uncommitted self-dependency I had named shipped in it. The verdict on the audited code (e0f8847) stands: published 0.2.25 is byte-identical to e0f8847 in every file except package.json, checked in round 2. The risk assessment in that sentence was wrong, though. The correct handling would have been to name the uncommitted self-dependency plainly in the handoff as a release risk that depended on Pipeman following the clone-based publish, not to dismiss it.
